items.name: hi_types
items.description: Header-only unit with the types shared by all units: status codes hi_status_t (HI_OK, HI_E_PARAM, HI_E_RANGE, HI_E_STATE, HI_E_BUSY, HI_E_REFUSED, HI_E_HW, HI_E_CRC), fault codes 1..9 (HI_FLT_*), entity ids (task index below HI_MAX_TASKS = 4, or HI_ENT_CODE, HI_ENT_CONFIG, HI_ENT_IWDG, HI_ENT_WWDG, HI_ENT_NONE), reset cause and supervisor state enumerations, the fault record, the retained fault state record (latch, nine counts, eight-entry history ring, fault count, fault-free ms accumulator) and the configuration table entry (name of at most 6 characters, period in ms, start and execution limits in time-base units of 10 us). It defines no function and holds no data.

items.name: hal_headers
items.description: Header-only unit declaring the hardware abstraction used by every other unit: critical section (hal_cpu.h), GPIO pins (hal_gpio.h, three pins), independent and window watchdog (hal_wdg.h), timer time base and one compare event (hal_timer.h), USART non-blocking transmit and receive (hal_usart.h), reset flags and reset request (hal_rcc.h), retained storage (hal_store.h), image and configuration read access (hal_mem.h) and task release (hal_task.h). No function is defined in src/; the port or driver project implements them and unit tests provide fakes (DEC-SWU-001). No unit touches a register or address.

items.name: crc32
items.description: Stateless software CRC-32/MPEG-2 (polynomial 0x04C11DB7, initial value 0xFFFFFFFF, no reflection, no final XOR, bytes in increasing address order). The running value is a context held by the caller, so one value over a range is produced from consecutive chunks. No state, reentrant; loop bounded by the checked length (at most 1 MiB = CRC32_MAX_LEN) times 8 bit steps.

functions.name: crc32_init
functions.behaviour: Returns 0xFFFFFFFF.

functions.name: crc32_update
functions.signature: uint32_t crc32_update(uint32_t ctx, const uint8_t *data, uint32_t len)
functions.behaviour: data non-NULL and 1 <= len <= 1048576: folds each byte into ctx MSB first with polynomial 0x04C11DB7 and returns the new context. data NULL, len 0 or len above 1048576: returns ctx unchanged. Executes len x 8 inner steps, no waiting.

items.name: config_manager
items.description: Owns the validated configuration table (SWC-SUP-050): a pointer to the linker-placed table and its entry count. States: UNINIT/INVALID (cfg_is_valid false, every accessor returns 0 or NULL) -> VALID after one successful cfg_init; a failed cfg_init leaves INVALID and notifies fault code 9 entity CONFIG. Accepted entry: name equal to one of the known task identities T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT, T_DIAG (CON-SUP-101, held as a constant table in the unit; any other name, including an empty or unterminated one, is an unknown task and is rejected as configuration fault 9, CON-SUP-115), period_ms a non-zero whole multiple of 10 ms with period_ms/10 <= 65535 (DEC-SWU-005, closes OP-SWC-005 and the width part of DEC-SWC-015), start and execution limit not longer than the period (limit in units of 10 us <= period_ms x 100). Count 1..4. Default data (SWC-SUP-001, SWC-SUP-050, CON-SUP-101, CON-SUP-103): src/config_defaults.c defines the constant table cfg_default_table[4] in release order T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT (10 ms, start limit 200 units = 2 ms, execution limit 300 units = 3 ms) and T_DIAG (100 ms, 200, 2000 units = 20 ms); the object's read-only data is placed by the linker script inside __cfg_start..__cfg_end and the build computes __cfg_crc over that block (DEC-SWU-010, OP-SWU-013); the port's hal_mem_cfg_table returns this table with count CFG_DEFAULT_COUNT. The table passes cfg_init. The table is read-only after validation. Call order: cfg_init once from the start-up manager after both CRC checks; accessors afterwards from the scheduler, timing supervisor and diagnostic communication.

functions.name: cfg_name_equal
functions.signature: static bool cfg_name_equal(const char *name, const char *known)
functions.behaviour: Compares name and known character by character over indices 0..6; returns false at the first differing character, true when both reach NUL at the same index. A name without NUL within indices 0..6 differs from every known name at index 6 (known names are at most 6 characters), so no read goes beyond index 6. Loop bounded by 7.

functions.name: cfg_entry_ok
functions.behaviour: Returns false when the name is not equal (cfg_name_equal) to any of the four known task names T_IN, T_CTRL, T_OUT, T_DIAG (unknown, empty or unterminated name), when period_ms is 0, not a multiple of 10, or period_ms/10 is above 65535, or when start_limit_u or exec_limit_u exceeds period_ms x 100; otherwise true. Loops bounded by 4 (known names) and 7 (name characters).

functions.name: cfg_init
functions.behaviour: Clears the previous table. table non-NULL, count 1..4 and every entry accepted by cfg_entry_ok: stores table and count, state VALID, returns HI_OK. Otherwise leaves INVALID, calls fm_notify(9, HI_ENT_CONFIG, ts_ms()) once and returns HI_E_RANGE.

functions.name: cfg_is_valid
functions.behaviour: Returns true after a successful cfg_init, false otherwise.

functions.name: cfg_count
functions.behaviour: Returns the entry count when VALID, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: cfg_get
functions.behaviour: VALID and task < count: pointer to the entry. Otherwise NULL.

functions.name: cfg_period_ticks
functions.behaviour: Valid task: period_ms / 10. Invalid task or table: 0.

items.name: time_service
items.description: Owns the timer through the HAL. Time base unit 10 us (wrapping 32 bit); milliseconds since the latest reset derived by integer division with a carried remainder, so the value never exceeds real elapsed time (ts_ms must be called at least every 40000 s; the control cycle calls it every 10 ms). Elapsed-time accounting (SWR-LAT-006): ts_elapsed_u gives a single conservative interval since a caller-held mark in 10 us units with no over-count; because the two readings are quantized and one unit is subtracted at every call, each call under-counts by less than 2 units (20 us), within the 100 us per-update limit of SWR-LAT-006. The subtraction is repeated at each call, so a sum of ts_elapsed_u results loses one unit (10 us) per call and is NOT bounded by the 10 ms per-reset limit; it is therefore not used for cumulative accounting. Cumulative operational-time accounting (SWR-LAT-006) takes the exact modular difference of ts_now_u readings in SWU-FLT-001, where the quantization telescopes and one unit is withheld once per interval. ts_ms differences are not used for intervals. Compare events: one slot per tag 0..32 (tag t < 16: start-limit event of task t; 16..19: execution-limit event of task t-16; 32: cycle end), each holding an instant; the HAL compare is always programmed to the earliest armed slot and cleared when none is armed (an instant already passed is due at once). ts_pop_due removes the earliest due slot, equal instants giving the lower tag first (start before execution before cycle end). Ordering range: an instant is ordered correctly relative to now only within the signed 32-bit distance, so ts_arm accepts instants at most TS_MAX_AHEAD_U units after the current reading and treats every earlier instant as due at once. Time origin: the counter value 0 is the latest reset (hal_timer.h contract), so ts_ms includes the time elapsed before ts_init (DEC-SWU-011, OP-SWU-014). All state changes run in the critical section of DEC-SWC-007. States: stopped -> running after ts_init.

functions.name: ts_diff
functions.signature: static int32_t ts_diff(uint32_t a, uint32_t b)
functions.behaviour: Returns (int32_t)(a - b), the signed wrapped distance; negative when a is before b.

functions.name: ts_reprogram
functions.behaviour: Reads the time; among armed slots picks the one with the smallest ts_diff(when, now) (lowest tag on equal distance) and calls hal_timer_set_compare with its instant; when no slot is armed calls hal_timer_clear_compare. Loop bounded by 33.

functions.name: ts_init
functions.behaviour: Disarms all slots, zeroes ms, remainder and the last reading (the time origin is counter value 0, the latest reset, DEC-SWU-011), calls hal_timer_start. HAL returns HI_OK: clears the compare and returns HI_OK; the first ts_ms call then counts all time from the reset to that call. HAL returns an error (10 us unit not realisable, OP-SWC-014): returns that status unchanged.

functions.name: ts_now_u
functions.behaviour: Returns hal_timer_read(), unit 10 us, wrapping at 2^32.

functions.name: ts_elapsed_u
functions.behaviour: mark_u NULL: returns 0. Otherwise reads the time base once, computes diff = (now - *mark_u) modulo 2^32 of the two quantized readings (unit 10 us) and returns diff - 1 when diff > 0, else 0, then stores now in *mark_u. Quantization: each reading floors the real instant to a unit, so the real interval T lies strictly between diff-1 and diff+1 units; the returned value is therefore never above T (no over-count) and below T by less than 2 units (20 us), within the 100 us per-update limit of SWR-LAT-006. The mark is the caller's previous reading, so no remainder is carried between updates and the unit withheld at each call is not recovered: a sum over n calls falls short of the real total by up to 2 units plus (n-1) units, so the function is for single intervals only, not for cumulative accounting (see SWU-FLT-001, which uses ts_now_u). The caller initialises the mark with one call whose result it discards (the first interval is then covered by the same per-call bound). Valid for intervals below 2^32 units (about 40000 s). Does not touch the ms count or remainder.

functions.name: ts_ms
functions.behaviour: In one critical section: adds (remainder + units since the last reading) / 100 to the ms count, keeps the remainder modulo 100, stores the reading, returns the ms count (wraps to 0 after 4294967295). Never above real elapsed time since reset, but the difference of two returned values can exceed the true interval by up to 1 ms, so it is a stamp and not an interval measure; interval accounting under SWR-LAT-006 uses ts_elapsed_u.

functions.name: ts_arm
functions.behaviour: tag > 32: returns HI_E_RANGE, nothing armed. Otherwise, in the critical section, ahead = ts_diff(instant_u, hal_timer_read()): ahead <= TS_MAX_AHEAD_U (0x3FFFFFFF units, about 3 h; a past instant, ahead <= 0, is due at once): arms or re-arms the slot, reprograms the HAL compare, returns HI_OK. ahead above TS_MAX_AHEAD_U: returns HI_E_RANGE, nothing armed. Scheduling horizon: instants at least 2^31 units ahead are indistinguishable from past ones, so callers must arm less than TS_MAX_AHEAD_U ahead; the callers do (limits are at most the period, at most 65535 ticks = 65535000 units, validated by cfg_init), the cycle event is 500 units ahead.

functions.name: ts_cancel
functions.behaviour: tag <= 32 and slot armed: disarms it, reprograms, returns true. Slot not armed (already decided or never armed) or tag > 32: returns false, no change.

functions.name: ts_pop_due
functions.behaviour: tag NULL: returns false. Otherwise, in the critical section, finds the armed slot with ts_diff(when, now_u) <= 0 and the smallest distance (lowest tag on equal distance); found: disarms it, stores its tag in *tag, reprograms, returns true; none due: returns false and *tag is unchanged. Loop bounded by 33.

attributes.rationale: F-sw-design-set-r3-003: the reset-relative origin (SWC-SUP-012, SWR-DIA-003) depends on a port fact the inputs do not give (timer runs from the latest reset and hal_timer_start preserves it). Substituting a different origin would not meet the requirement, so the fact is recorded as blocking OP-SWU-014 instead of being assumed silently; the port or a human decision must answer it.

items.name: output_control
items.description: Sole owner of the two control outputs and the status signal through hal_gpio (pins CTRL1, CTRL2, STATUS). Data: the safe-state-commanded flag. States: after oc_init flag clear, pins low; oc_safe_state sets the flag (until the next oc_init, i.e. the next reset) and drives all pins low; oc_status_high is the only call that drives a pin high and only the status pin. The control outputs are never driven high. Ordering (DEC-SWC-010): the flag check, the fault-state read (fm_get_state) and the status pin write of oc_status_high, and the flag set and pin writes of oc_safe_state, are each one critical section, so no interleaving leaves the status pin high after a safe-state command. oc_init is the first start-up step; oc_status_high is called once by the start-up manager.

functions.name: oc_init
functions.behaviour: Calls hal_gpio_config_output_low for pins 0, 1 and 2 (all three are always attempted), clears the safe-state flag. Returns HI_OK when all three succeeded, HI_E_HW when any failed.

functions.name: oc_safe_state
functions.behaviour: In one critical section sets the flag and writes all three pins low (write results ignored: the command is idempotent and repeated by the next call). Callable from task and interrupt context; bounded by three HAL writes.

functions.name: oc_status_high
functions.behaviour: In one critical section reads fm_get_state: flag set, or state SAFE or LATCHED: returns HI_E_REFUSED with no pin changed. Otherwise writes the status pin high; HAL failure returns HI_E_HW, success HI_OK.

items.name: wdg_service
items.description: Sole owner of the independent watchdog (100 ms timeout) and window watchdog (window 6 ms to 12 ms) and of the inhibit flag, through hal_wdg. States: ws_init clears the flag and the window-enabled state; the flag is set only by ws_inhibit and cleared only by the next ws_init after a reset. Every service or refresh runs as one critical section that reads the flag and, only when clear, issues the HAL command, so no command follows a seen-set flag (SWR-WDG-001). The window watchdog is enabled by the first ws_cycle_service call (enable instant treated as the previous refresh, DEC-SWC-005) and refreshed by each later call at the same fixed phase; ws_startup_service services only the independent watchdog and is called between CRC chunks. The decision depends only on the flag, never on application data.

functions.name: ws_init
functions.behaviour: Clears the inhibit flag and the window-enabled state; returns HI_OK.

functions.name: ws_activate
functions.behaviour: Calls hal_wwdg_configure(6, 12); on success calls hal_iwdg_start(100) and returns HI_OK when that succeeded. Any HAL refusal returns HI_E_HW (the independent watchdog is not started after a refused window configuration).

functions.name: ws_startup_service
functions.behaviour: In one critical section: flag clear: calls hal_iwdg_service; flag set: nothing is issued.

functions.name: ws_cycle_service
functions.behaviour: In one critical section: flag set: nothing issued, returns HI_OK. Flag clear: window not yet enabled: calls hal_wwdg_enable, success sets enabled (returns HI_OK), refusal returns HI_E_HW and enabling is retried at the next call; window enabled: calls hal_wwdg_refresh. In the flag-clear case hal_iwdg_service is called in the same section.

functions.name: ws_inhibit
functions.behaviour: Sets the flag (single atomic word write, never masked); idempotent; no way to clear until reset.

functions.name: ws_is_inhibited
functions.behaviour: Returns the flag.

items.name: fault_manager
items.description: Single receiver of every detection and owner of the retained fault state (SWC-SUP-054: latch, nine detection counts indexed code-1, eight-entry history ring oldest at hist_head, fault count, fault-free ms) and of the volatile state (operational flag, safe flag, reset-armed mask, hold flag of the time accounting, and a pending-report FIFO queue of FM_PEND_CAP = 36 entries (code, entity, detection ms) with head, length and a saturating lost-report counter). All read-modify-write runs in the critical section of DEC-SWC-007 and the retained state is written through hal_store after each change. State derived: LATCHED (latch, priority) > SAFE (a detection since reset) > OPERATIONAL (fm_set_operational) > STARTUP. Path A (codes 1 to 7, 9): detection counted, latch at the third detection or at once for code 9, otherwise software reset armed for that code; fault-free time zeroed; the report is then submitted (queued on BUSY). Every detection is counted and reported; the safe-state reaction (watchdog inhibit, then outputs low) is issued only at the first detection since reset (safe flag still clear), as SWC-SUP-006 and DEC-SWC-017 require, so each further detection of a coincident pass costs only the count, the retained write and the report submission and omits the two reaction calls. Path B (code 8): report submitted only; nothing counted, no safe state. Report event (fm_report_done): history append, fault count +1; code 8: count +1 and latch at the third; codes 1 to 7 with an armed reset and latch clear: software reset requested through the reset request service. fm_init: power-on cause clears the retained state; any other cause with fully valid content keeps it; otherwise (non-power-on cause, any part invalid) the parts that pass their own check (hal_store_read_parts of SWU-FLT-002: header part and each history slot) are kept and stay readable through fm_snapshot, invalid parts start empty, the latch is set and the loss is recorded: code 9 entity CONFIG is appended to the history when a slot is free, and when all eight entries are valid none is overwritten and the loss is recorded as one more code 9 detection count (DEC-SWU-004, OP-SWU-001). Concurrency (SWR-WDG-001): in path A (first detection) and in the latching code 8 completion the safe flag, the watchdog inhibit and the output safe-state command are issued inside the same critical section that counts the detection (the safe flag is set there for every detection, so a later detection finds the reaction already issued and the inhibit and safe state persist until reset), so no watchdog service of SWU-WDG-001 (which checks the flag in its own critical section) can follow a detection; critical sections nest (the critical-section HAL returns the previous state). Operational accounting (SWR-LAT-006; time reading ts_now_u of SWU-TIM-001 in 10 us units, 100 units per ms; ts_elapsed_u is not used because it withholds one unit at every call, which would lose 10 us per update): each update adds the exact modular difference of two readings to a carried sub-ms remainder, so the quantization of the readings cancels over the interval (telescoping sum) and nothing is lost per update; one unit (10 us) is withheld once per interval (hold flag, consumed at the first update with a non-zero difference) because the difference of two quantized readings can exceed the real time by less than one unit, so the credited time never exceeds the real time. Shortfall at any instant: at most 2 units (20 us) plus the carried remainder below 1 ms, within 100 us per update (no loss per update) and 10 ms per reset (SWR-LAT-006). The interval starts at the transition to OPERATIONAL (fm_set_operational), and a code 8 completion that zeroes the fault-free time also starts a new interval (fm_restart_interval), so start-up time and time before the event is never counted. The difference is exact for update spacing below 2^32 units (about 11.9 h). Pending reports: a report answered BUSY is appended to a bounded FIFO queue of FM_PEND_CAP = 36 entries (twice the 18 report sources: codes 1 to 3 per task, codes 4 to 9 once), so every detection of a coincident pass (at most 8 limit events of DEC-SWC-017 plus the flow, CRC and configuration detections of the same cycle, each source at most twice) stays reported; no entry is overwritten. Arrival and service bound (SWC-SUP-008 submission within 10 ms): arrivals are limited by the detectors (each source recurs at most once per control cycle or once per start-up or CRC pass, and after the first detection a software reset or the latch ends the pass), the 36-entry queue is sized at twice the 18 sources, and the queue is drained by fm_retry_pending at every transmit step; a report is stored without delay on BUSY, so the submission instant is the detection instant whenever the queue has room (submission is the synchronous acceptance into the diagnostic ring of DC_QUEUE_SLOTS = 20 lines or, on BUSY, into this queue, both inside the detector's call; the 10 ms deadline therefore never depends on transmission time, which only drains the queues). Admission capacity: 20 diagnostic slots plus 36 pending entries hold 56 reports, against at most 36 arrivals under the stated arrival bound (18 sources, each at most twice per pass). The 'twice per source' bound is not derivable from the inputs (a detector may recur once per control cycle until the reset or watchdog ends the pass), so overflow cannot be excluded by design alone. This is an argument, not a proof: whether coincident detections plus a line in progress can exceed the diagnostic line's capacity within 10 ms is the requirement-level question OP-SWC-013, carried as OP-SWU-012. The full-queue path is a counted last resort: the new report is not stored and a saturating lost-report counter (fm_pending_lost) is incremented; the detection itself stays counted and its safe-state effect is unaffected. fm_retry_pending resubmits the head entry and removes it only after a submission that is not BUSY; entries are only appended at the tail (interrupt or task) and only removed at the head (fm_retry_pending, the single consumer), so an append during a submission never disturbs the head. Call order: fm_init once at start-up after the reset classification; fm_cycle_update once per control cycle.

functions.name: fm_zero
functions.behaviour: Sets latch, history length and head, fault count, fault-free ms, all nine counts and all eight history entries to zero. Loops bounded by 9 and 8.

functions.name: fm_hist_append
functions.signature: static void fm_hist_append(uint8_t code, uint8_t entity, uint32_t ms)
functions.behaviour: Caller holds the critical section. History shorter than 8: writes at (head + length) mod 8 and increments the length. History full: overwrites the oldest entry at head and advances head modulo 8.

functions.name: fm_header_ok
functions.signature: static bool fm_header_ok(const hi_retained_t *loaded, uint16_t parts)
functions.behaviour: Returns true when bit HS_VALID_HEADER of parts is set, loaded->hist_len <= 8 and loaded->hist_head < 8; false otherwise. No side effect.

functions.name: fm_salvage
functions.signature: static void fm_salvage(const hi_retained_t *loaded, uint16_t parts, bool hdr)
functions.behaviour: Zeroes the retained state, then: hdr true: copies latch, fault-free ms and the nine counts, and walks the history from loaded head for loaded hist_len entries, appending (oldest first, through fm_hist_append) each entry whose slot bit (1 + slot) is set in parts. hdr false: counts, latch and fault-free ms stay zero and every slot 0..7 whose bit is set is appended in slot order. Entries with a clear bit are dropped. Loops bounded by 9 and 8.

functions.name: fm_restart_interval
functions.behaviour: Takes the current ts_now_u reading as the accumulation mark, zeroes the sub-ms remainder and sets the hold flag (one 10 us unit to be withheld at the next non-zero difference). No other state is changed.

functions.name: fm_submit
functions.signature: static void fm_submit(uint8_t code, uint8_t entity, uint32_t ms)
functions.behaviour: Calls dc_submit_fault. Result other than HI_E_BUSY: nothing is kept. Result HI_E_BUSY: in the critical section, queue length below 36: stores code, entity and ms at slot (head + length) mod 36 and increments the length (nothing already queued is changed); queue full: the report is not stored and the lost-report counter is incremented, saturating at 255.

functions.name: fm_init
functions.behaviour: Reads the retained state through hal_store_read_parts (parts mask, invalid parts zero) and classifies the header with fm_header_ok; clears operational and safe flags, the reset mask, the pending queue (head, length and lost counter zero); starts an accumulation interval with fm_restart_interval. cause POR: retained state zeroed and hal_store_clear called, returns HI_OK. Other cause, header usable and parts == HS_VALID_ALL: content used unchanged, HI_OK. Other cause, anything else (blank store, invalid header or any invalid history slot): fm_salvage keeps the individually valid parts, latch set; history shorter than 8: entry (9, HI_ENT_CONFIG, 0) appended; history full (all 8 entries valid): nothing in the history is overwritten and the loss is recorded as one more code 9 detection count (saturating at 255), the latch and the fault count; fault count = loaded fault count + 1 (saturating) when the header is usable, otherwise the history length after the loss handling (8 when the history was full); returns HI_E_STATE. Writes the state back through hal_store_write.

functions.name: fm_set_operational
functions.behaviour: In the critical section, latch clear and not yet operational: starts the accumulation interval with fm_restart_interval (so start-up time is never counted) and sets the operational flag. Latch set or already operational: no change.

functions.name: fm_notify
functions.signature: hi_status_t fm_notify(uint8_t code, uint8_t entity, uint32_t detect_ms)
functions.behaviour: Code outside 1..9, or code 1..3 with entity >= 4: treated as code 9 entity HI_ENT_CONFIG and the final result is HI_E_RANGE. Code 8: only fm_submit (no count, no output change, no inhibit). Other codes, in this order: critical section {first = safe flag clear on entry; count of the code saturating at 255; count >= 3 or code 9: latch set and the reset-armed bit cleared, otherwise reset-armed bit set; fault-free ms and sub-ms remainder zeroed; safe flag set; retained state written; only when first is true: ws_inhibit() then oc_safe_state()} all in one critical section (no watchdog service can be ordered after the detection); then fm_submit outside it. Every detection is counted and reported; the safe-state reaction is issued for the first detection since reset only (a second and later detection, including those of one coincident pass, calls neither ws_inhibit nor oc_safe_state). Returns HI_OK for a valid code.

functions.name: fm_report_done
functions.signature: void fm_report_done(uint8_t code, uint8_t entity, uint32_t detect_ms)
functions.behaviour: Code outside 1..9: ignored. Otherwise in the critical section: history append (code, entity, detect_ms) and fault count +1. Code 8: count of code 8 +1 (saturating), fault-free ms zeroed and a new accumulation interval started with fm_restart_interval, latch set when the count is >= 3 (then ws_inhibit and oc_safe_state inside the same section). Other codes: when the reset-armed bit of the code is set it is cleared and, with the latch clear, su_request_reset() is called after the section. Retained state written.

functions.name: fm_retry_pending
functions.behaviour: Up to 36 rounds: in the critical section copies code, entity and ms of the head entry; queue empty: stops. Calls dc_submit_fault outside the section; HI_E_BUSY stops the loop and keeps the entry; any other result: in the critical section the head advances modulo 36 and the length decreases by one. Reports appended meanwhile by fm_submit go to the tail and do not affect the head.

functions.name: fm_pending_lost
functions.behaviour: Returns, in one critical section, the number of reports not stored because the pending queue was full since fm_init (saturating at 255; 0 when none was lost).

functions.name: fm_cycle_update
functions.behaviour: In the critical section reads ts_now_u, forms delta = now - mark (10 us units, exact modulo 2^32) and advances the mark to now. Only when operational, latch clear and no detection since reset: when the hold flag is set and delta > 0, delta is reduced by one unit and the flag cleared (done once per interval); low = (delta mod 100) + carried remainder (remainder below 100 units); whole ms = delta / 100 + low / 100; new remainder = low mod 100, carried to the next update. The credited time is the sum of the exact differences minus one unit, so it is never above the real elapsed time, and it lags the real time by at most 2 units (20 us) plus the carried remainder below 1 ms; no unit is lost per update, so 6000 updates in 60 s lose nothing beyond that, within the 100 us per update and 10 ms per reset limits of SWR-LAT-006; whole ms added to the fault-free ms (saturating at 4294967295); reaching 60000 clears all nine counts and the accumulator (remainder kept); retained state written. Otherwise only the mark was advanced and the remainder is zeroed. The computation cannot overflow 32 bits.

functions.name: fm_get_state
functions.behaviour: Latch set: HI_STATE_LATCHED; else safe flag: HI_STATE_SAFE; else operational flag: HI_STATE_OPERATIONAL; else HI_STATE_STARTUP. Read in one critical section.

functions.name: fm_is_latched
functions.behaviour: Returns true when the latch is set.

functions.name: fm_fault_count
functions.behaviour: Returns the fault count since the last power-on reset.

functions.name: fm_snapshot
functions.behaviour: out NULL: returns 0. Otherwise copies the history oldest first into out[0..n-1] in one critical section and returns n (0..8, 0 for an empty history).

attributes.rationale: F-sw-design-set-r2-003: submission (acceptance into the diagnostic ring or this queue) is synchronous with detection, so the 10 ms deadline does not depend on drain time; capacity is 20 + 36 = 56 reports. Whether arrivals can exceed that during a line in progress cannot be excluded or bounded from the inputs: it is the product-level question OP-SWC-013, already carried as OP-SWU-012 (blocking); rework cannot answer it, and the lost-report counter keeps any overflow observable. Rework of F-sw-design-item-r3-001, -002, -004: the safe-state reaction is issued at the first detection since reset only; the time accounting uses ts_now_u differences with a single withheld unit instead of ts_elapsed_u (which lost one unit per update); pending reports use a 36-entry FIFO queue with a lost counter instead of one overwritable cell per source. OP-SWU-008 is closed by this change. F-sw-design-set-r3-001: the arrival and transmission bound depends on the coincident-report deadline choice (OP-SWC-013, carried as blocking OP-SWU-012); no bound or requirement is invented here, and the coverage findings that name SWU-FLT-001 (STK-SUP-010..013, SWC-SUP-002 and the listed scenarios) stay open until that decision. The cost of hal_store_write in the further-detection path is carried in OP-SWU-009.

items.name: hal_store_ex
items.description: Header-only part split from SWU-FLT-001: the per-part retained-storage read hal_store_read_parts (include/hal_store_ex.h), which refines the retained storage driver interface SWC-SUP-026 so that individually valid parts survive a failed whole-record check. The driver checks the header part (bit 0: latch, counts, history length and head, fault count, fault-free ms) and each of the eight history slots (bit 1 + slot) separately, returns zero for parts that fail, and returns the validity mask (0 = nothing valid). The function is implemented outside src/ (DEC-SWU-001); unit tests provide a fake. It defines no function and holds no data. Used only by fm_init of SWU-FLT-001.

items.name: timing_supervisor
items.description: Owns the per-task supervision state (SWC-SUP-051): release, start and completion instants (unit 10 us, validity flags), consecutive missed-period counter, alive-on flag. Instants are wall-clock instants stamped from ts_now_u inside the critical section, so preemption lengthens a measured time (DEC-SWU-006, OP-SWU-005). Events: tsup_on_release (scheduler, before the task is made ready) evaluates the ending period when alive supervision is on and a previous release exists: completed when a completion instant is stored and is not before the previous release instant, counter reset, otherwise +1; counter reaching 2 raises fault code 1 once. It then records the release, invalidates start and completion, cancels the task's execution event and arms its start-limit event at release + start limit + 1 unit. tsup_on_start decides late start (code 2, start - release > start limit) only if its start event was still pending, then arms the execution event at start + execution limit + 1 unit. tsup_on_complete decides overrun (code 3, completion - start > execution limit) only if the execution event was still pending. tsup_on_compare (timer handler) raises code 2 when the release has no start stored, code 3 when the start has no completion stored. A value equal to the limit is within it. Faults are notified after the critical section so it stays short. Call order per task period: release, start, completion.

functions.name: tsup_init
functions.behaviour: Clears all instants, validity flags and counters of the four entries and switches alive supervision off; returns HI_OK.

functions.name: tsup_enable_alive
functions.behaviour: In the critical section clears the release-valid flag and the missed counter of every entry and sets alive-on, so the first release afterwards only starts the period.

functions.name: tsup_on_release
functions.behaviour: Task not configured (cfg_get NULL): returns HI_E_RANGE, no change. Otherwise in the critical section: alive-on and a previous release stored: completed = completion valid and (completion - previous release) as signed >= 0; completed: counter 0, else counter +1 (saturating at 255); fault 1 pending when the counter equals 2. Records now as release, clears start-valid and done-valid, ts_cancel of the execution tag, ts_arm of the start tag at now + start_limit + 1. After the section, fault 1 pending: fm_notify(1, task, ts_ms()). Returns HI_OK.

functions.name: tsup_on_start
functions.behaviour: Task not configured: HI_E_RANGE. No release stored: HI_E_STATE. Otherwise in the critical section stores now as the start instant; ts_cancel of the start tag returns true and (now - release) > start limit: late. ts_arm of the execution tag at now + exec_limit + 1. After the section, late: fm_notify(2, task, ts_ms()). Returns HI_OK. A start whose event is no longer pending raises nothing.

functions.name: tsup_on_complete
functions.behaviour: Task not configured: HI_E_RANGE. No start stored: HI_E_STATE. Otherwise in the critical section stores now as the completion instant; ts_cancel of the execution tag returns true and (now - start) > exec limit: overrun. After the section, overrun: fm_notify(3, task, ts_ms()). Returns HI_OK.

functions.name: tsup_on_compare
functions.behaviour: tag < 16: start-limit event of task = tag; 16 <= tag < 32: execution-limit event of task = tag - 16; other tags and tasks >= 4: ignored. Start event: release stored and no start stored: fm_notify(2, task, ts_ms()). Execution event: start stored and no completion stored: fm_notify(3, task, ts_ms()). A stored instant means the start or completion event already decided: nothing raised.

items.name: flow_supervisor
items.description: Owns the checkpoint log of the current control cycle (SWC-SUP-052): the released tasks in configured release order and the checkpoints received in arrival order, at most four each, plus an overflow indication set when a checkpoint arrives with the log full. Order per cycle: fsup_cycle_begin at the tick (called by the scheduler with the tasks it released), fsup_checkpoint once per task execution from task context, fsup_cycle_end at the cycle-end phase; the check stays at the cycle end for every task (OP-SWC-011 upstream, not decided here). The log is cleared by fsup_cycle_end.

functions.name: fsup_init
functions.behaviour: Clears expected list, log and overflow indication; returns HI_OK.

functions.name: fsup_cycle_begin
functions.behaviour: tasks NULL with count != 0: HI_E_PARAM. count > 4 or any listed task >= 4: HI_E_RANGE. In both cases state unchanged. Otherwise in the critical section stores the list, clears the log and the overflow indication, returns HI_OK (count 0 is valid).

functions.name: fsup_checkpoint
functions.behaviour: task >= 4: HI_E_RANGE. Log full (4 entries): sets the overflow indication in the critical section, returns HI_E_RANGE, log unchanged. Otherwise appends task in the critical section and returns HI_OK.

functions.name: fsup_cycle_end
functions.behaviour: In the critical section compares the log with the expected list position by position: the first position i where the log is shorter or differs is a fault with entity = expected[i]; with no such position and more checkpoints than expected, or the overflow indication set (a checkpoint arrived with the log full), the fault has entity HI_ENT_NONE. Clears log, expected list and overflow indication. After the section, fault: fm_notify(4, entity, ts_ms()) once. No fault: nothing.

items.name: scheduler
items.description: Timer-driven scheduler (control-cycle part A). Holds a 16 bit tick counter per table entry (DEC-SWU-005) and the start-up permission. The task set, periods and order are read from the validated configuration table only; no task name or period is coded here. States: NOT_PERMITTED (after sch_init) -> PERMITTED (sch_permit, which makes every entry due at the next tick). At each sch_tick, in table order, a counter is incremented (saturating) and a task whose counter reached its period in ticks is released: tsup_on_release (alive evaluation and release instant), then, only if the supervisor is not SAFE or LATCHED (checked and released in one critical section against interrupt-context detection), hal_task_release; after the first detection no further task is released. The released list is handed to the flow supervisor. Called once per 10 ms tick by the control-cycle task.

functions.name: sch_blocked
functions.behaviour: Returns true when fm_get_state is HI_STATE_SAFE or HI_STATE_LATCHED.

functions.name: sch_init
functions.behaviour: Zeroes the four tick counters and clears the permission; returns HI_OK.

functions.name: sch_permit
functions.behaviour: Sets every counter to 0xFFFF (due at the next tick) and sets the permission.

functions.name: sch_tick
functions.behaviour: Not permitted, no valid configuration (cfg_count 0) or sch_blocked: returns HI_E_STATE and releases nothing. Otherwise for each entry in table order: counter +1 (saturating at 0xFFFF); counter >= cfg_period_ticks: counter 0 and tsup_on_release; on HI_OK, one critical section (hal_cpu_enter_critical / hal_cpu_exit_critical, fault-detection interrupts masked) holds the final sch_blocked check and the release: not blocked: the task index is appended to the released list and hal_task_release is called inside the section; blocked: nothing is released and the walk stops after the section is left. A detection in interrupt context during the section takes effect after it, so no release follows a detection that was already visible. Then fsup_cycle_begin with the released list; returns HI_OK. Loop bounded by the entry count (at most 4).

items.name: rt_checker
items.description: Run-time code integrity check (SWC-SUP-053 state: segment cursor and running CRC context, single calling context). One segment of at most 1024 bytes of the application image (region from hal_mem, end byte excluded) per control cycle in increasing address order; the context is initialised at the first segment of a pass and carried unchanged across segments; the last segment of a pass holds the remaining bytes; after the last segment the whole-range value is compared with the reference word and the next pass starts at the first segment. A mismatch notifies fault code 7 entity CODE. Called once per control cycle by the control-cycle part B after the flow check.

functions.name: rtc_init
functions.behaviour: Sets the cursor to 0 and the context to the initial CRC value; returns HI_OK.

functions.name: rtc_check_pass
functions.behaviour: ctx equal ref: HI_OK. Otherwise fm_notify(7, HI_ENT_CODE, ts_ms()) and returns HI_E_CRC.

functions.name: rtc_step
functions.behaviour: Region NULL or length 0: fm_notify(7, HI_ENT_CODE, ts_ms()), cursor 0, returns HI_E_RANGE. Otherwise a cursor at or beyond the length restarts at 0; cursor 0 initialises the context; the segment is min(1024, length - cursor) bytes updated into the context through crc32_update and the cursor advances. When the cursor reaches the length the result of rtc_check_pass(context, hal_mem_app_ref_crc()) is returned and the cursor returns to 0; otherwise HI_OK.

items.name: diag_comm
items.description: Diagnostic communication on the USART, owner of the report queue and buffers (SWC-SUP-056): a FIFO ring of 20 slots (1 + 6 + 3 x 4 + 1, SWC-SUP-039), a 40 character transmit line buffer, a 32 character request buffer, the answer state and an eight-entry history snapshot. Submission never blocks: a full ring answers HI_E_BUSY and nothing is dropped or overwritten. dc_service_step is the one non-blocking step, called by the diagnostic task every 1 ms and by the start-up task between CRC chunks (one caller at a time, DEC-SWC-011): it resubmits pending reports (fm_retry_pending), receives at most 64 characters, then moves the line in transmission. A new line is started from the queue first (oldest report), otherwise from the active answer, so a report due during an answer line is sent after that line and before further answer lines, and a started line is never interrupted. Lines: RST,<cause>; FLT,<code>,<entity>,<ms>; STS,<state>,<fault count>; GET FAULTS answers one FLT line per history entry oldest first and then always a final END line (END alone when the history is empty; at most 8 FLT lines plus END, CON-SUP-134); ERR. Every accepted report submission calls hal_diag_task_ready (include/hal_diag_wake.h, DEC-SWU-009) after the queue write and its critical section, so the diagnostic task is made ready at once (SWC-SUP-039, DEC-SWC-015); a BUSY submission queues nothing and does not call it. A line is complete when its line feed was handed over and the USART reports transmit complete; for a fault report the fault manager is then notified (report event). Requests: a line ending with line feed; exactly GET STATUS, GET FAULTS or GET RESET are answered, any other, longer than 32 characters or damaged by a receive error answers ERR; a request received while an answer is active or in transmission is ignored. Answer content (state, count, history snapshot) is fixed at reception.

functions.name: dc_put_char
functions.signature: static uint8_t dc_put_char(uint8_t pos, uint8_t ch)
functions.behaviour: pos < 39: stores ch at pos in the line buffer and returns pos + 1. Otherwise returns pos unchanged (space for the line feed is kept).

functions.name: dc_put_str
functions.signature: static uint8_t dc_put_str(uint8_t pos, const char *text)
functions.behaviour: Appends characters of text up to its NUL or 40 characters examined, through dc_put_char; returns the new length.

functions.name: dc_put_u32
functions.signature: static uint8_t dc_put_u32(uint8_t pos, uint32_t value)
functions.behaviour: Appends value in decimal without leading zeros (0 gives "0"), at most 10 digits; returns the new length.

functions.name: dc_finish_line
functions.behaviour: Stores the line feed at pos, sets the line length to pos + 1 and the transmit position to 0, marks a line as in transmission. pos is at most 39.

functions.name: dc_entity_name
functions.behaviour: entity < 4: the configured task name, or "" when cfg_get is NULL. HI_ENT_CODE: "CODE"; HI_ENT_CONFIG: "CONFIG"; HI_ENT_IWDG: "IWDG"; HI_ENT_WWDG: "WWDG". Any other value (including HI_ENT_NONE): "".

functions.name: dc_render_rst
functions.behaviour: Renders RST,<name> with name POR, IWDG, WWDG, SW or OTHER for cause 0..4; a cause above 4 renders OTHER.

functions.name: dc_render_flt
functions.signature: static void dc_render_flt(uint8_t code, uint8_t entity, uint32_t ms)
functions.behaviour: Renders FLT,<code>,<entity name>,<ms decimal> and finishes the line; an empty entity name leaves the field empty.

functions.name: dc_render_answer
functions.behaviour: Renders the next line of the active answer: STATUS gives STS,<state name>,<count>; RESET gives RST,<cause>; FAULTS gives the FLT line of snapshot entry number next while next is below the snapshot length, and END when next equals the snapshot length (the last line of every GET FAULTS answer, also for an empty snapshot); any other kind ERR. Marks the line as an answer line, advances the answer index and ends the answer (kind NONE) after the last line.

functions.name: dc_start_line
functions.behaviour: Pops the oldest queue slot in the critical section; a slot gives an FLT or RST line and returns true. No slot and an active answer: renders the next answer line, true. Otherwise false.

functions.name: dc_tx_step
functions.behaviour: No line in transmission and none could be started: returns. Characters left: hal_usart_write of the rest, the accepted count (clamped to the rest) advances the position. Position at the end and hal_usart_tx_complete true: the line ends; a fault report line calls fm_report_done(code, entity, ms) of its slot. Never waits.

functions.name: dc_rx_equals
functions.behaviour: True when the assembled request has exactly the length and characters of text; false otherwise (no read beyond the text).

functions.name: dc_request_done
functions.behaviour: An answer is active or an answer line is in transmission: ignored. Otherwise: damaged or overlong line gives ERR; GET STATUS stores state (fm_get_state) and count (fm_fault_count), one line; GET FAULTS stores the snapshot (fm_snapshot) and sets the number of answer lines to snapshot length + 1 (the FLT lines then END; 1 line, END, for an empty snapshot); GET RESET one line; anything else ERR.

functions.name: dc_rx_step
functions.behaviour: Up to 64 times: hal_usart_read; HI_E_STATE stops; any other error marks the line damaged; a line feed completes the request (dc_request_done) and clears the buffer and damage mark; otherwise the character is stored while fewer than 32 are held, a 33rd character marks the line overlong (damaged).

functions.name: dc_push
functions.behaviour: In the critical section: fewer than 20 slots queued: appends the slot at the tail and sets the result HI_OK; ring full: result HI_E_BUSY, no slot changed. After leaving the critical section, on HI_OK only, calls hal_diag_task_ready exactly once (never inside the critical section, never waits, no other state touched); on HI_E_BUSY it is not called. Returns the result. Callable from task and interrupt context.

functions.name: dc_init
functions.behaviour: Empties the queue, buffers and answer state, sets the recorded reset cause to OTHER, calls hal_usart_configure; returns HI_OK or HI_E_HW when the configuration fails.

functions.name: dc_submit_rst
functions.behaviour: cause above HI_RST_OTHER: HI_E_RANGE, nothing queued. Otherwise queues an RST slot through dc_push: HI_OK (the cause is recorded for GET RESET and the diagnostic task is made ready by hal_diag_task_ready) or HI_E_BUSY when the ring is full (no wakeup).

functions.name: dc_submit_fault
functions.signature: hi_status_t dc_submit_fault(uint8_t code, uint8_t entity, uint32_t ms)
functions.behaviour: code outside 1..9: HI_E_RANGE, nothing queued. Otherwise queues an FLT slot through dc_push: HI_OK (the diagnostic task is made ready at once by hal_diag_task_ready, so the first character is handed over within the 1 ms bound of SWC-SUP-063) or HI_E_BUSY when full (no wakeup; the submitter repeats on the next 1 ms run). Callable from task and interrupt context.

functions.name: dc_service_step
functions.behaviour: Calls fm_retry_pending, dc_rx_step and dc_tx_step in that order; never waits; bounded by 64 receive reads and one transmit write.

functions.name: dc_is_idle
functions.behaviour: True when no slot is queued and no line is in transmission.

items.name: startup_manager
items.description: Start-up sequence (task SWC-SUP-060) and reset request service (SWC-SUP-038). su_run order: (1) oc_init before anything else; (2) ts_init and dc_init; reset of the supervision units; (3) read and clear the reset flags, classify, take the classification instant; fm_init; (4) ws_activate (a refusal is reported as fault code 9 entity CONFIG); (5) RST message submitted, then for an independent or window watchdog reset fault code 8 notified, so RST precedes the code 8 line in the FIFO; when the RST submission fails (queue still full at the time bound, or another error) code 8 is still notified for a watchdog reset (SWC-SUP-002 step 4: the code 8 report is required also then; it is queued by the fault manager when the diagnostic queue is busy), the integrity checks are skipped, no task is released, and the barrier (9) still runs, so a code 8 report is always attempted and either completes or ends in a reset; (6) a set latch skips the integrity checks and ends start-up without release, but only after the barrier (9) has completed the watchdog-reset report (RST and code 8 lines); (7) image CRC over hal_mem_app_region against its reference (fault 5 entity CODE) and, only when the image check passed, configuration block CRC (fault 6 entity CONFIG); a code 5 fault stops the check sequence: the configuration CRC and cfg_init are not run, the report barrier (9) still runs after a watchdog reset, and start-up ends with HI_E_STATE and no release; each region is cut into 1024 byte chunks with a diagnostic transmit step and an independent-watchdog service after every chunk (DEC-SWU-003, closes OP-SWC-004 conditionally on OP-SWC-012); (8) when both passed, cfg_init on the table from hal_mem (a failure is fault 9); (9) after a watchdog reset, report barrier: transmit until the queue is idle, with the independent-watchdog service issued only while the wait has lasted at most SU_REPORT_WAIT_MS = 80 ms (DEC-SWU-005); a transmission not complete by then gets no further service, so the independent watchdog (100 ms timeout) resets; the wait is ended only by completion or by elapsed time, SU_REPORT_ABORT_MS = 200 ms; no iteration count ends it (the count of consecutive unchanged ms readings, saturating at SU_WAIT_MAX_STEPS = 100000, only withholds the watchdog service while the time base does not advance, and resumes at the next changed reading, so it cannot cut off a healthy transmission whatever the iteration speed; a dead time base is therefore ended by the unserviced independent watchdog); if the queue is still not idle at the time bound, su_request_reset is called (DEC-SWU-008), so the barrier ends in completion, in a reset or in a watchdog reset and never in a release (on a host fake the call returns and the barrier reports failure); (10) when all checks passed and the state is neither SAFE nor LATCHED and the status-high request is accepted: alive supervision on, scheduler permitted, OPERATIONAL. Otherwise su_run returns HI_E_STATE and no task is released. Reset classification priority IWDG, WWDG, POR, SW, OTHER (DEC-SWU-004, OP-SWU-002).

functions.name: su_classify
functions.behaviour: Bit IWDG set: HI_RST_IWDG; else WWDG: HI_RST_WWDG; else POR: HI_RST_POR; else SW: HI_RST_SW; no recognised bit: HI_RST_OTHER.

functions.name: su_check_region
functions.signature: hi_status_t su_check_region(const uint8_t *base, uint32_t len, uint32_t ref, uint8_t code, uint8_t entity)
functions.behaviour: base NULL or len 0: HI_E_RANGE. Otherwise CRC-32/MPEG-2 in chunks of at most 1024 bytes; after every chunk dc_service_step and ws_startup_service. Value different from ref: HI_E_CRC. Either error calls fm_notify(code, entity, ts_ms()). Equal: HI_OK. Loop bounded by len / 1024 + 1.

functions.name: su_request_reset
functions.behaviour: Calls hal_rcc_request_reset (does not return on the target) and returns HI_OK.

functions.name: su_wait_continues
functions.signature: static bool su_wait_continues(uint32_t start_ms, uint32_t *last_ms, uint32_t *same)
functions.behaviour: Reads ts_ms once. Reading equal to *last_ms: increments *same, saturating at SU_WAIT_MAX_STEPS (100000); the count never ends the wait. Reading different: stores it in *last_ms and zeroes *same. Returns false only when (reading - start_ms), unsigned 32-bit, is above SU_REPORT_ABORT_MS (200); otherwise true. No loop. Pointers are internal callers' locals and are not NULL-checked.

functions.name: su_submit_rst
functions.signature: static bool su_submit_rst(hi_reset_cause_t cause, uint32_t ms)
functions.behaviour: Reads ts_ms at entry. Repeats: dc_submit_rst; HI_OK returns true; HI_E_BUSY runs dc_service_step and su_service_while_progressing(entry instant), then retries while su_wait_continues is true; any other result returns false. su_wait_continues false (200 ms elapsed): false. Loop bounded by elapsed time; on a dead time base by the unserviced independent watchdog (no service while the unchanged-reading count is at SU_WAIT_MAX_STEPS).

functions.name: su_wait_reports
functions.behaviour: Reads ts_ms at entry. While dc_is_idle is false and su_wait_continues is true: dc_service_step, su_service_while_progressing(entry instant, unchanged-reading count), then re-evaluates dc_is_idle. Returns true when dc_is_idle() is true at the end. If the loop ended on su_wait_continues (200 ms elapsed since entry) with dc_is_idle() still false: calls su_request_reset (hal_rcc_request_reset, which does not return on the target; the code 8 count and the latch are untouched) and then returns false, which only a host fake can observe. Once more than SU_REPORT_WAIT_MS ms (unsigned 32-bit difference, wrap-safe) have elapsed since entry no watchdog service is issued, so a stalled transmission lets the independent watchdog (100 ms timeout) reset well before the 200 ms bound. A healthy transmission is never cut off: a full diagnostic queue drains in about 70 ms (DEC-SWU-005) and no iteration count ends the wait.

functions.name: su_service_while_progressing
functions.signature: static void su_service_while_progressing(uint32_t start_ms, uint32_t same)
functions.behaviour: If ts_ms() - start_ms (unsigned 32-bit) is at most SU_REPORT_WAIT_MS (80) and same is below SU_WAIT_MAX_STEPS (the time base advanced within the last 100000 checks): calls ws_startup_service. Otherwise issues nothing. No loop, no wait.

functions.name: su_run
functions.behaviour: Runs the sequence of the description. oc_init, ts_init or dc_init failing: returns HI_E_HW at once. su_submit_rst returning false: code 8 is still notified for a watchdog reset, the image and configuration checks and cfg_init are skipped, the barrier runs when the cause was a watchdog reset, HI_E_STATE and no release. Latch set after the code 8 notification: the image and configuration checks and cfg_init are skipped, the barrier runs when the cause was a watchdog reset (so the RST and code 8 lines are transmitted to completion or end in a reset), no release, HI_E_STATE. su_check_region on the image failing (code 5): the configuration region check and cfg_init are skipped, the barrier runs when the cause was a watchdog reset, HI_E_STATE. Any check, configuration validation, ws_activate, RST submission or barrier failing: no release, HI_E_STATE. State LATCHED or SAFE, or oc_status_high refusing: HI_E_STATE. Otherwise tsup_enable_alive, sch_permit, fm_set_operational and HI_OK.

attributes.rationale: F-sw-design-item-r3-005: a code 5 fault now stops the check sequence (SWC-SUP-002), skipping the configuration CRC and cfg_init. F-sw-design-set-r1-001: a failed RST submission no longer skips the code 8 notification (SWC-SUP-002 step 4 requires it after every watchdog reset); the report is queued by the fault manager and the barrier decides completion or reset. The RST line is not re-sent, so its order before code 8 holds only when the RST was accepted. F-sw-design-set-r1-002: the waits are bounded by elapsed time (SU_REPORT_ABORT_MS) instead of an iteration count. F-sw-design-set-r2-001: the unchanged-reading count no longer ends a wait or requests a reset (no execution-time bound for one iteration is available in the inputs); it only withholds the watchdog service while the time base does not advance, so progress decides and a healthy wait is never cut off. F-sw-design-set-r2-002: a set latch no longer returns right after one transmit step; the integrity checks are skipped but the barrier still completes the watchdog-reset report before su_run returns without release. F-sw-design-item-r1-012: the RST submission and the barrier no longer service the watchdog unconditionally; service stops after SU_REPORT_WAIT_MS (DEC-SWU-005), so a stalled transmission is not kept alive and the watchdog resets as SWC-SUP-002 requires. The diagnostic unit exposes no progress counter, so the criterion is elapsed time against the full-queue drain time.

items.name: cycle_task
items.description: Bodies of the control-cycle task (SWC-SUP-061) and the timer event handler (SWC-SUP-062). Part A runs at the 10 ms tick: scheduler release, then the cycle-end compare event is armed at tick instant + 500 units (5 ms, DEC-SWU-002, closes OP-SWC-002), after the 3 ms execution limits of the 10 ms tasks and before the 12 ms window limit. The handler body decides every compare event due or falling due during the pass in expiry order (at most 16 per entry), start and execution events through the timing supervisor, and reports whether the cycle-end event was taken so the caller makes part B ready. Part B at the cycle end: flow check, one run-time CRC segment, fault-free time update, watchdog cycle service (refresh at the same phase every cycle). Both parts and the handler never wait. Coincident events (DEC-SWC-017, SWC-SUP-006): every due limit event of the pass, also when the supervisor is already SAFE or LATCHED, is decided by the timing supervisor so its detection is counted and its report is pending; the handler itself never skips a decision. Not repeating the safe-state reaction after the first detection is a fault manager matter (OP-SWU-008). A refused window-watchdog enable in part B is a fault (code 9, entity WWDG) with the safe-state reaction.

functions.name: cyc_part_a
functions.behaviour: Reads the tick instant, calls sch_tick, arms the cycle-end event (tag 32) at tick instant + 500. Arming refused: returns HI_E_RANGE. Otherwise returns the scheduler result (HI_OK, or HI_E_STATE when no release was allowed; the cycle-end event is armed in both cases).

functions.name: cyc_part_b
functions.behaviour: In order: fsup_cycle_end, rtc_step, fm_cycle_update, ws_cycle_service. The results of fsup_cycle_end and rtc_step are ignored (faults are already notified by the callee). ws_cycle_service returning HI_E_HW (window-watchdog enable refused; the independent watchdog was still serviced in that call): fm_notify(HI_FLT_CONFIG, HI_ENT_WWDG, ts_ms()) is called, so the fault manager enters the safe state, latches (code 9), inhibits both watchdogs and reports; the independent watchdog then resets the device, so operation never continues without the window watchdog. Any other ws_cycle_service result: no further action.

functions.name: cyc_timer_handler
functions.behaviour: Up to 16 times: ts_pop_due at the current time; none due ends the loop; the cycle-end tag sets the result true; any other tag always calls tsup_on_compare, whatever the supervisor state (also SAFE or LATCHED), so every due limit event is decided and, when it detects a fault, counted and reported by the fault manager. The handler never suppresses a decision. Returns true when the cycle-end event was taken in this pass.

attributes.rationale: F-sw-design-item-r1-011: refused window-watchdog enable is now notified (code 9, entity WWDG, the entity the architecture lists for code 9 range) and leads to inhibit. F-sw-design-item-r2-001: SWC-SUP-006 and DEC-SWC-017 require each due limit event to be decided with its detection count and report; the handler therefore calls tsup_on_compare for every limit event and no longer reads the fault state. Omitting the repeated safe-state reaction belongs to fm_notify (SWU-FLT-001, outside this item), see OP-SWU-008.

items.name: fault_inject
items.description: Fault-injection test hook, excluded from the production build (SWC-SUP-013). The exclusion is defined by two reviewable build configurations: hi/sw-design/build/production.mk compiles the source list of hi/sw-design/build/sources.mk, which does not contain src/fault_inject.c, and stops with an error if that file is ever added to the production list; hi/sw-design/build/test.mk compiles the same list plus src/fault_inject.c. The exclusion is established by reading those files; it has not been executed here, and the generic compile gate (which compiles every src/**/*.c) does not evidence it. Each injection presents the detection condition of one fault class to the detector concerned so the real detection, reaction and report path runs: 1 three releases without completion with alive on; 2 a release and its start-limit event with no start; 3 release, start and the execution-limit event with no completion; 4 a cycle with one released task and no checkpoint; 5 and 6 a region check against a reference that differs from the computed CRC; 7 a pass comparison with unequal values; 8 the code 8 notification for an independent watchdog reset (the only direct fault manager call); 9 an invalid configuration table (the held table becomes invalid).

functions.name: fi_alive
functions.behaviour: tsup_enable_alive, then three tsup_on_release calls; returns the last result.

functions.name: fi_late_start
functions.behaviour: tsup_on_release, then tsup_on_compare of the start tag of the task; returns the release result.

functions.name: fi_overrun
functions.behaviour: tsup_on_release, then (when it returned HI_OK) tsup_on_start, then tsup_on_compare of the execution tag; returns the first error or HI_OK.

functions.name: fi_flow
functions.behaviour: fsup_cycle_begin with the single task, then fsup_cycle_end with no checkpoint; returns the begin result.

functions.name: fi_region
functions.signature: static hi_status_t fi_region(uint8_t code, uint8_t entity)
functions.behaviour: Calls su_check_region on a one-byte sample with a reference that differs from its CRC; returns HI_E_CRC.

functions.name: fi_inject
functions.behaviour: Codes 1 to 4 with task < 4: the condition above. Codes 1 to 4 with task >= 4, or a code outside 1..9: HI_E_RANGE, nothing injected. Code 5 and 6: fi_region with entity CODE or CONFIG. Code 7: rtc_check_pass(0, 1). Code 8: fm_notify(8, HI_ENT_IWDG, ts_ms()). Code 9: cfg_init(NULL, 0). Returns the detector result.

attributes.rationale: F-sw-design-item-r1-014: no build definition existed, so the earlier claim of verification by inspection was unsupported and is withdrawn. hi/sw-design/build/{sources,production,test}.mk now define the two configurations; the write scope does not allow a root Makefile, hence this location. Whether the project's gates use the production list is for the conductor and inspector to judge.

decisions.text: All functions declared in include/hal_*.h are implemented outside src/ (target port or driver project); unit tests provide fakes. The abstract reset bits of hal_rcc.h and the 10 us time unit are mapped by the port. No unit contains a register name, offset or fixed address.
decisions.rationale: Keeps every unit host-testable with -Iinclude only (DEC-SWC-001).

decisions.text: The cycle-end compare event and the fixed phase of the flow check and the watchdog cycle service are 500 time units (5 ms) after the tick instant (CYC_PHASE_U).
decisions.rationale: Closes OP-SWC-002 as a design value: later than the 3 ms execution limit of the 10 ms tasks plus the detection latency, earlier than the 12 ms window limit, and fixed so refresh instants are one control period apart. The numeric priority scheme belongs to the integration of the tasks and is not coded in the units.

decisions.text: The start-up CRC chunk is 1024 bytes (SU_CHUNK_BYTES), the same size as the run-time segment; a diagnostic transmit step and an independent watchdog service follow every chunk.
decisions.rationale: Closes OP-SWC-004 as a design value. It meets the 1 ms transmit-step interval and the 100 ms service interval only under the condition of DEC-SWC-016 (CRC cycles per byte and core clock, OP-SWC-012, upstream and blocking); no feasibility is claimed here.

decisions.text: During the start-up report waits (RST submission, report barrier) the independent watchdog is serviced only while at most SU_REPORT_WAIT_MS = 80 ms have elapsed since the wait began (ts_ms, unsigned difference); later no service is issued and the watchdog resets.
decisions.rationale: No progress counter is exposed by the diagnostic unit. A full queue (DC_QUEUE_SLOTS = 20 lines of at most 40 characters at about 87 us per character, about 70 ms) drains within 80 ms, so a healthy transmission is never cut off, while the last service is at most 80 ms after the wait began and the 100 ms watchdog resets a stalled one. Timing rests on the architecture's transmit figures; the target check is left to integration.

decisions.text: Reset classification priority is IWDG, WWDG, POR, SW, then OTHER. After a non-power-on reset with invalid retained content the latch is set and the loss is recorded in the history as code 9 with entity CONFIG.
decisions.rationale: The architecture names the five causes and the recording of the loss but not a priority for several bits set at once nor a code for the loss; the watchdog-first order never clears retained state on an ambiguous reading, and code 9 entity CONFIG is the nearest defined code. See OP-SWU-001 and OP-SWU-002.

decisions.text: The scheduler tick counter is 16 bit, so a period is accepted up to 65535 ticks (655350 ms); the configuration entry stores the period in ms, limits in time units of 10 us and a name of at most 6 characters; entries are in release order; an entry violating any of these is a configuration fault code 9.
decisions.rationale: Closes OP-SWC-005 (counter width and period encoding) and OP-SWC-008 (name length, so a report line is at most 24 characters with the default names) as design values, in line with DEC-SWC-015 and DEC-SWC-014.

decisions.text: Start, completion and release instants are wall-clock instants from the time base, so any preemption of a task between its start and completion event is part of the measured execution time.
decisions.rationale: Implements what SWC-SUP-006 specifies (stored instants); the requirement-level treatment of preemption (OP-SWC-016 upstream) is not decided here, see OP-SWU-005.

decisions.text: When the report barrier passes SU_REPORT_ABORT_MS (200 ms) with the diagnostic queue still not idle (no iteration count ends the barrier; a dead time base is ended by the independent watchdog, which is not serviced while the ms reading is unchanged for SU_WAIT_MAX_STEPS checks), su_wait_reports requests a reset through su_request_reset (hal_rcc_request_reset). The barrier therefore ends only by completion or by a reset (on the target the independent watchdog, no longer serviced after SU_REPORT_WAIT_MS, resets earlier); su_run never releases after an incomplete report.
decisions.rationale: SWC-SUP-002 requires completion, failure notification or reset; an unbounded loop breaks the bounded-loop rule and returning to the caller leaves behaviour unspecified. A reset request is the reset outcome the architecture names, reached deterministically when the step bound is hit.

decisions.text: The USART HAL has no transmit-failure indication; a failure notification for a report therefore does not exist in the units. The start-up barrier is bounded by elapsed time and, earlier, by the independent watchdog reset when no progress is made.
decisions.rationale: The USART driver interface (SWC-SUP-024) defines partial acceptance only; no failure path is invented.

decisions.text: Stack estimates per unit (stack_bytes_max) are estimates from the deepest call chain of the unit alone; the deepest chain of the control-cycle task is fm_notify -> oc_safe_state -> HAL and fm_notify -> dc_submit_fault, the start-up chain su_run -> su_check_region -> dc_service_step -> dc_tx_step -> fm_report_done -> su_request_reset. No numeric budget is given by the inputs (OP-SWC-010).
decisions.rationale: No recursion and no dynamic allocation are used, so every chain is statically bounded.

decisions.text: The diagnostic-task wakeup is the HAL function void hal_diag_task_ready(void) declared in include/hal_diag_wake.h (owned by SWU-DIA-001). It makes the diagnostic task ready at once, never waits, is callable from task and interrupt context and is implemented outside src/ by the target port (the scheduler integration); diag_comm calls it once after every accepted submission, outside the critical section. Its own latency is part of the 0.2 ms-plus-0.8 ms first-character bound of SWC-SUP-063 and is not evaluated in the units.
decisions.rationale: SWC-SUP-039 and DEC-SWC-015 require the submission to make the diagnostic task ready at once; hal_task_release of hal_task.h releases application tasks by table index and is not used for the supervisor's own task.

decisions.text: The default configuration table is the constant cfg_default_table in src/config_defaults.c (four tasks, defaults of CON-SUP-101 and CON-SUP-103). The linker script places that object's read-only data in the block __cfg_start..__cfg_end and the build computes the reference word __cfg_crc over the block; the port's hal_mem_cfg_table returns the table and CFG_DEFAULT_COUNT. No compiler extension is used for the placement.
decisions.rationale: SWC-SUP-001 and SWC-SUP-050 require linker-placed default data under the block CRC. The linker script and the CRC build step are outside src/ and are not verified here (OP-SWU-013).

decisions.text: The time origin of ts_ms is counter value 0 of the timer HAL, defined as the latest reset; hal_timer_start must not set the counter back. ts_arm refuses instants more than TS_MAX_AHEAD_U (0x3FFFFFFF units, about 3 h) after the current reading, so the signed wrapped distance orders every accepted instant against now.
decisions.rationale: SWC-SUP-012 and SWR-DIA-003 require milliseconds since the latest reset, including the time before initialisation. Whether the target counter runs from reset is a port fact not given by the inputs (OP-SWU-014). The horizon is far above the longest armed interval (65535000 units).

open_points.text: After a non-power-on reset with invalid retained content, SWC-SUP-026 asks that entries which still pass an individual check stay readable for diagnosis. The retained-storage HAL here returns only a validity flag for the whole content, so the per-entry check, and the code used to record the loss (code 9 entity CONFIG chosen in DEC-SWU-004), are not decided.

The inputs do not give how several reset flags set at once map to one cause, nor how the target's reset flags map to the abstract bits of hal_rcc.h; the port and the reference manual section and page (CON-SUP-002 names none) are needed. The priority IWDG, WWDG, POR, SW is a design choice (DEC-SWU-004).

When start-up ends with a set latch or a fault, su_run returns HI_E_STATE and the idle behaviour of the start-up task (whether it services the independent watchdog while the diagnostic task runs, or lets the watchdog reset) is not stated by the architecture and is not coded in the units.

OP-SWC-006 (reference manual section and page for GPIO access, atomicity of a pin write, pin state from reset to initialisation) is carried to the port: the units reach the pins only through hal_gpio.h and rely on neither property.

A further detection of a coincident pass still performs the count, one hal_store_write and the report submission in fm_notify; the 5 us allocation of DEC-SWC-017 for a further decision depends on the execution time of hal_store_write and dc_submit_fault on the target, which the inputs do not give. The design omits the watchdog inhibit and the output safe-state call after the first detection; the measured cost is to be checked on the target or simulator.

Whether the execution time measured for the overrun decision includes preemption by higher-priority work (OP-SWC-016) is a requirement-level choice; the units measure wall-clock start to completion (DEC-SWU-006).

OP-SWC-011 (upstream, blocking) is unresolved: T_DIAG has a 20 ms execution limit but is released in a 10 ms control cycle, and the inputs do not say whether a T_DIAG checkpoint not yet reported at that cycle end is a flow fault or is evaluated when its limit expires. The flow check currently evaluates the tasks released in the cycle at the cycle end (CON-SUP-104 read literally) and can report a timely T_DIAG as a missing checkpoint. The product authority must choose; the flow and timing design then follows.

OP-SWC-012 (upstream, blocking) is unresolved: the core clock, the CRC throughput and the execution times are not given, so the execution-time, processor-time and simulator-integration assumptions (including DEC-SWU-003 chunk size and the 80 ms and 200 ms start-up wait figures) are not substantiated at design level.

OP-SWC-013 (upstream, blocking) is unresolved: whether coincident detections with a report line in progress may exceed the 10 ms report deadline, or a started line may be abandoned, is a requirement-level choice. The 36-entry pending queue and its arrival argument (SWU-FLT-001) hold only within that choice; the lost-report counter records any report that does not fit.

The linker script that places the read-only data of src/config_defaults.c inside __cfg_start..__cfg_end, and the build step that computes __cfg_crc over the block, are outside src/ and outside the inputs of this stage; the placement and the CRC value are to be confirmed at integration.

Whether the target timer counter runs from the latest reset (value 0) and hal_timer_start leaves it running is a port fact not given by the inputs (OP-SWC-014 concerns the unit); ts_init relies on that contract (DEC-SWU-011). The reset-relative timestamp of SWC-SUP-012 and SWR-DIA-003 cannot be stated correctly without this fact, so it blocks.
